paperTitle: Caturama VR: An English-Localized Virtual Reality Serious Game for Brazilian Folklore
centralContribution: This paper presents "Caturama VR," an English-localized Virtual Reality (VR) serious game developed for the Meta Quest 2, designed to immerse players in Brazilian folklore and legends, featuring an indigenous protagonist Caturama, an optimized VR interface, dynamic inventory management, and visually captivating special effects. The work details the game's advanced 3D graphics, narrative interaction, and comprehensive pre-user VR testing by the development team, which significantly enhanced interaction quality, gameplay balance, immersion, presence, and overall performance.

elements.name: Abstract Summary
elements.description: Despite VR's potential for immersive cultural heritage experiences, its application in exploring cultural heritage remains largely untapped. VR game development faces challenges such as hardware limitations, high costs, user comfort issues (motion sickness, eye strain), content creation complexity, intuitive UI design, and technical hurdles like latency. Existing digital games incorporating Brazilian folklore often lack deep VR integration or focus on simpler mechanics. This paper addresses these gaps by creating "Caturama VR," a VR experience that deeply embeds Brazilian folklore into interactive gameplay and decision-making processes, aiming to promote cultural heritage in an immersive manner.
elements.justification: Provides the foundational context, problem, and purpose of the paper as a summary of the abstract content.
